collection.description: Two children have invented their own secret language, and an adult politely asks what one word means.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) and (friend) have invented their own language. It has about forty words, most of which mean "food," and a special word for "grown-ups are coming." They've been using it all day, and the grown-ups are going slightly mad trying to work it out. (grownup), an adult, has just asked, very politely, what "blim-blim" means.

text_only.reason: food in the story (a meal, a snack, a basket of fruit); the village's stores do not change

a.name: Answer A
a.text: "It means 'crab,'" says (subject). "But only a big one," adds (friend). "A small one is a blim." (grownup) nods seriously, and from then on says "blim-blim" whenever (grownup.he/she) sees a big crab. The children are both delighted and horrified. Their secret language is not so secret anymore. They start inventing a new one that very afternoon.

b__fx.name: Answer B
b__fx.text: (subject) and (friend) look at each other. "Snorrok," says (subject). "Snorrok," agrees (friend). They walk off together, giggling. (grownup) never finds out what "blim-blim" means. Nobody ever finds out what "snorrok" means. Possibly not even the children.
